title: Microsoft Entra: account recovery through government ID verification (Web)
summary: Hold: tenants using the earlier preview must enable the new policy to continue recovery, contrary to the assurance that existing behaviour does not change. The profile creation API does not document user-group assignment, and the credential-cleanup description omits important success conditions.

claims.claim: Account recovery restores organisational account access when all registered authentication methods are unavailable.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes identity verification and trust re-establishment before replacement of authentication methods rather than simple credential recovery.
claims.quote: account recovery focuses on identity verification and trust re-establishment prior to replacement of authentication methods rather than simple credential recovery

claims.claim: Account recovery enablement and TAP issuance are under Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview).
claims.quote: Go to Entra ID > Account recovery. Open Settings (preview). Use Actions after recovery in Account recovery settings to choose how users register replacement methods.

claims.claim: Profile configuration is under Microsoft Entra admin center > Verified ID > ID verification profiles > Profiles.
claims.quote: Go to Verified ID > ID verification profiles > Profiles. Select the profile name to open its configuration, or choose the action you need: Create profile.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/verifiedId/profiles provides automation for the row's user scope, provider, purpose and mode.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph verifiedIdProfile assign groups include exclude recovery profile users scope'; read create-profile, verifiedIdProfile, verifiedIdUsageConfiguration and verifiedIdProfileConfiguration v1.0 references. They document creation and configuration, not group assignment.
claims.fix: Keep 'POST /v1.0/identity/verifiedId/profiles', but replace the row note with 'This call creates the profile, not its user-group assignment or the tenant policy. verifiedIdProfileConfiguration.acceptedIssuer sets the issuer; verifiedIdUsageConfigurations.purpose sets Recovery and isEnabledForTestOnly sets evaluation or production. Configure user scope through the admin UI.' The create reference is https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/identityverifiedidroot-post-profiles?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: Users start recovery by selecting Recover your account at sign-in.
claims.quote: If you're unable to sign in with any methods, select Recover your account.

claims.claim: The organisation selects the provider to which the user is redirected.
claims.quote: You're redirected to the identity proofing service configured by your organization, and you start the identity proofing process.

claims.claim: The provider verifies government-issued identification.
claims.quote: The provider verifies government-issued identification documents using advanced fraud detection.

claims.claim: Face Check verifies the user's presence against the ID photo.
claims.quote: Account recovery first verifies proof of presence by comparing the photo on the user's government-issued ID to a real-time Face Check.

claims.claim: The user presents the resulting Verified ID to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: The user presents their newly acquired Verified ID to Microsoft Entra ID. The system validates the credential's authenticity.

claims.claim: Successful recovery issues a TAP by default.
claims.quote: By default, the user receives a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) with limited validity and is guided through registering new authentication methods, such as passkeys.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Evaluation mode tests verification without recovering accounts.
claims.quote: Evaluation — Users can test the identity verification flow to confirm it works correctly. Accounts are not recovered in this mode.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Production mode allows verified users to recover independently and re-enrol authentication methods.
claims.quote: Production — Users who complete identity verification can fully recover their accounts, receive a Temporary Access Pass by default, and re-enroll authentication methods. Users recover accounts independently without waiting for help desk availability.

claims.claim: An optional custom authentication extension validates verified claims against organisational records.
claims.quote: Verified claims from the identity verification provider are passed to the extension, which validates them against organizational data such as a human resources information system (HRIS) or an employee directory.

claims.quote: Account recovery uses automated identity proofing to reduce reliance on manual help desk verification.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that social engineering can manipulate support staff into granting access.

claims.claim: Nothing in the sources says existing behaviour changes on arrival.

Qualify the preceding no-action statement as applying to tenants that have not used the earlier preview.
